tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

scope-time-dependent-bi-invariant-cost: Abstract, p.1: the authors state what they compute (bi-invariant cost of explicitly time-dependent Hamiltonians, Nielsen framework, regularised norms). Matches the value.
setup-quantity-computed-is-total-cost: Section I p.4 and Section V E pp.19-20: the authors state they compute the total cost along the given curve, not a minimum, because the curve is not a geodesic of the bi-invariant geometry. Both quotes are in context.
setup-systems-infinite-dim-one-dimension: Section I p.3 (explicit time dependence, infinite-dimensional Hilbert space) and Section III p.7 ('All the systems considered in this paper are one-dimensional').
def-bi-invariant-schatten-cost: Section II p.6 Eq. (10)-(11): the paper fixes the cost it uses (Schatten norm with p=2, trace of the squared Hamiltonian, Cartan-Killing length). The Schatten and Cartan-Killing facts are cited ([39,40,48,49]) but the value reports the cost the paper adopts.
def-regularisation-condition-mean-value: Section III p.6 Eq. (12): the paper names Tr(H - lambda I)=0 'the regularization condition' and notes that subtracting a multiple of the identity does not alter the geometry (U(1) shift).
driving-force-as-trace-regulator: Appendix A 1, pp.24-25: the unitary transformations (A2), the transformed Hamiltonian (A3) and the regulator condition (A4) are worked out in the paper, and the cost is shown equal to Eq. (23). The constant force does not change the cost value.
isotonic-mean-value-either-sign: Appendix A 2, p.25: Eqs. (A6)-(A10) derive the mean value (symbols lost in text layer); the text states it can be positive or negative depending on the singular term strength. Direct consequence of the shown formula.
otf-norm-needs-offdiagonal-elements: Section IV C p.11 Eqs. (42)-(47) and Section VII p.23: the off-diagonal part enters Eq. (45) and the minus sign in Eq. (47) lowers the cost for real frequency. The no-stationary-eigenstates remark is the paper's stated motivation. Condition: real frequency, stated in Section IV A.
otf-sign-choice-fixed-by-ho-limit: Section IV C p.11: the paper states the condition it imposes (reduce to the HO result at constant frequency) and the resulting choice of the negative sign. A statement of its own procedure.
otmf-su11-algebra: Section V B p.16 Eqs. (77)-(81) and Appendix C p.26: the generators K+, K0, K- and their commutation relations are given explicitly, the two forms of U follow from the group structure, and Appendix C derives the decomposition by a 2x2 matrix representation.
equivalence-otf-otmf-time-reparametrisat: Section V C pp.17-18, Eqs. (84)-(91): the time change dtau = dt/m1 is applied to the auxiliary equation, Eq. (86), and to the SU(1,1) functions, Eqs. (89)-(91). The wavefunction map is only 'easily checked'. Condition stated: the integral in Eq. (84) can be done and inverted.
equivalence-total-cost-otf-otmf: Section V D p.18, Eqs. (92)-(94): the cost integrals are changed by the reparametrisation using Eq. (88), and the equality is shown. Condition: the time change of Eq. (84), with the same start and end operators.
equivalence-norms-and-bounds-do-not-map: Section V D point 3 p.19: the authors state that only the integrals map, not the norms, and the bounds Eqs. (51) and (76) do not map; they trace it to the extra factor in Eq. (88). A caveat on their own equivalence.
efficiency-proposal-future-work: Section V E p.20: the authors propose an efficiency (geodesic distance over path length, bi-invariant geometry) and defer it ('study this further in a future work'). States what the paper does not cover.
quench-profile-setup: Section VI p.20, Eq. (97): constant frequency Omega0 up to t=0, then decreasing continuously toward zero; the authors name it the end-critical protocol. The profile is taken from [65], stated as the paper's example.
future-directions-limits: Section VII p.24: the authors state classically chaotic systems and invariant geometry under general time-dependent unitaries as open problems for future work. States what the paper does not cover.
parisi-bn-definition: Section 2 p.2: the paper defines a Bayesian network as a graphical representation of probability distributions with three components (nodes, directed edges, probabilities), and a node as a proposition fixing a variable's value. Matches the value.
qci-unconv-definition: 'Computing in new and creative ways', p.2: the lesson gives its working definition and says it is kept informal.
qci-unconv-not-minor-variants: p.2: the lesson says multi-processor and trinary-variable machines are not very unconventional and says what it is most interested in (no clear CPU). States the scope of the term as used in the lesson.
qci-unconv-scope-of-lesson: p.2: the lesson says it does not cover the whole field and focuses on efforts relevant to the company's products and practically useful. All three quotes are in one passage.
qci-unconv-probabilistic-definition: 'Probabilistic Computers', pp.5-6: the lesson says 'We will call this a probabilistic computer', defines it against the deterministic computer, and explains why it avoids 'non-deterministic'.
qci-unconv-digital-analog-definition: 'Analog and Continuous-time Computers', p.6: the lesson defines digital (discrete 1 and 0, forbidden voltage ranges) and analog (continuous allowed states). The claim that conventional computers use voltage ranges is a field description, but the terms are defined here.
qci-unconv-medium-math-caveat: Header note, p.1: 'some math doesn't render correctly on Medium' and the full equations are on the company site. A limit the page states about this version.
reservoir-computing-definition: 'Reservoir Computing' section: the page gives its definition of the term (randomly initialised network, then a simple linear model on the processed data).
dataset-ravdess: 'Dataset' section: the page states it uses RAVDESS (1440 files, 24 speakers, 8 emotions) and the goal of detecting the emotion.
split-by-actor-random: 'Setting up the parameters' code cell: NUM_ACTORS=24, NUM_TRAIN_ACTORS=19, random.shuffle(ACTORS), first 19 for training; the loading cell sends other actors' files to the test set. No seed is set, which the value does not claim.
preprocessing-cochleagram: 'Convert audio data to a cochleagram' code: signal[50001:125000], resample to 12e3 Hz, Lyon passive ear with decimation_factor=77 (DECIMATION_FACTOR) and ear_q=8.
qci-applications-emucore-reservoir-confi: 'Connecting to EmuCore' code cell: VBIAS=0.3, GAIN=0.65, NUM_NODES=800, NUM_TAPS=NUM_NODES, FEATURE_SCALING=0.5, DENSITY=1, NUM_F=77.
reservoir-maps-77-to-800: 'Connecting to EmuCore' code cell: the input has 77 columns (assert), process_all_data runs, and the output is asserted to have NUM_NODES=800 columns.
readout-linear-regression: 'Create a Linear Regression Model' cell: LinearRegression(fit_intercept=True), labels *2-1 repeated per time step, score on the training data. Matches the value.
prediction-and-metric: 'Process Training Data' and WSR_MSE cells: prediction is the mean of the time-step outputs, a file is correct when argmax hits the true class, wsr=success/count. The filters on repetition, statement and intensity admit all values (both 01 and 02), so they do not change the metric.

theory_low.time-independent-geodesic-constant-gener: Section III B p.8: the geodesic-from-constant-generator fact is cited to [50] and [40], not proved here. A cited result.
theory_low.otf-compact-cost-formula: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3, Eqs. (30)-(31), p.9: the diagonal and non-diagonal matrix elements of the time-dependent-frequency Hamiltonian that the compact cost formula is built from are taken from [43]: 'The derivations of the above expressions ... can be found in [43], and we do not repeat it here for brevity.' The cost formula rests on that cited derivation. Gray: the cited step is a ladder-operator computation the paper outlines.
theory_low.otf-constant-frequency-limit: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3, p.9 onward: the constant-frequency limit is read off the compact cost formula, whose matrix elements (Eqs. (30)-(31)) are taken from [43] without derivation ('we do not repeat it here'). Transitive on otf-compact-cost-formula. Gray, as there.
theory_low.otf-total-cost-upper-bound: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3: the Cauchy-Schwarz step is background, but it is applied to the compact cost formula, whose matrix elements (Eqs. (30)-(31), p.9) are taken from [43] without derivation. Transitive on otf-compact-cost-formula. Gray, as there.
theory_low.otf-time-lower-bound-speed-limit: Section IV C p.12, Eq. (52): a formal rearrangement of the bound, with no separate proof. The quantum-speed-limit link is only an analogy ('often appears'), and the paper cites [54] where such a bound is conjectured.
theory_low.example1-norm-prop-freq-squared: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3 example 1: the norm is evaluated from the compact cost formula, whose matrix elements (Eqs. (30)-(31), p.9) are taken from [43] without derivation. Transitive on otf-compact-cost-formula. Gray, as there.
theory_low.example1-total-cost-log-growth: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3 example 1: the total cost is integrated from the compact cost formula, whose matrix elements (Eqs. (30)-(31), p.9) are taken from [43] without derivation. Transitive on otf-compact-cost-formula. Gray, as there.
theory_low.example1-special-case-not-only-frequency: Section IV D Case-2 p.13, Eq. (58): the norm contains a factor G(t), so it is not proportional to Omega^2 even though the text says it is, and the sentence contradicts itself. The total cost is 'lengthy' and not shown. The value repeats an internally inconsistent statement.
theory_low.example2-vanishing-schwarzian-norm: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 3 example 2: the norm is evaluated from the compact cost formula, whose matrix elements (Eqs. (30)-(31), p.9) are taken from [43] without derivation. Transitive on otf-compact-cost-formula. Gray, as there.
theory_low.otmf-unitary-equivalence-time-independen: Section V A p.14: the first half (time-independent unitary gives equal norms) is solid, but the second half (a time-dependent unitary breaks invariance) is asserted with 'would' and no derivation here. The value carries both halves.
theory_low.otmf-norm-formula-and-bound: Section V A p.15, Eqs. (71)-(76): the formula uses cited matrix elements [58]. The bound Eq. (76) is given by 'a similar procedure' without steps, and holds only if the second term is non-positive (positive frequency and a0>0), a condition the value drops.
theory_low.equivalence-not-from-unitary-invariance: Section V D point 2 p.19: the claim that the two Hamiltonians are not related by any time-independent unitary is asserted, not shown. The remark that the equivalence follows from the definition of the evolution operator is an explanation, not a proof.
theory_low.equivalence-time-dependent-unitary-not-c: Section V D p.19: the connection by time-dependent unitaries is cited to [61], and the non-equivalence of the costs follows only from the assertion (not derived) that the cost is not invariant under time-dependent unitaries.
theory_low.geodesic-constant-generator-for-otmf-cur: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 2, p.8: 'the geodesic is generated by a constant generator [50]' is cited, not proved here. The sibling item time-independent-geodesic-constant-generator, which states the same cited fact, is already graded low; this item uses it for the OTMF curve and should match.
theory_low.cost-constants-numerical-only: Sections IV C-IV D pp.11-13: the 'only overall magnitude' remark is made for Case-1, where both terms scale as Omega^2. In general c21 and c22 multiply different terms of Eq. (47), so the ratio can change the time dependence. The value overgeneralises; the series value is not given.
theory_low.caldirola-kanai-cost-time-independent: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Sec. 4, Eq. (68), p.15: the diagonal and non-diagonal matrix elements used for the Caldirola-Kanai cost are 'respectively given by [58]', and the auxiliary-equation solutions come from [55] and [58] (p.13). The time-independence result rests on those cited inputs. Gray: the cited step is a ladder-operator computation.
theory_low.qci-unconv-bit-flip-superposition-exampl: pp.7-8: a worked illustration with no theorem and no proof. The state definition did not render in the text layer, and the measurement probabilities are the standard Born rule, stated not proved.
